passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The Registrants face various risks associated with their businesses. Our businesses, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks. In addition, this report also contains forward-looking and other statements about our businesses that are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties. See "Forward-Looking Information," "Item 1. Business," "Item 7. Combined Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and Note 12 to the Financial Statements for additional information concerning the risks described below and for other risks, uncertainties and factors that could affect our businesses and financial results. As used in this Item 1A., the terms "we," "our" and "us" generally refer to PPL and its consolidated subsidiaries taken as a whole, or PPL Electric and its consolidated subsidiaries taken as a whole within the Pennsylvania Regulated segment discussion, LG&E, KU and their consolidated subsidiaries taken as a whole within the Kentucky Regulated segment discussion, and RIE within the Rhode Island Regulated segment discussion. Order of Subsection Presentation A. Risks Related to Registrant Holding Company B. Risks Related to Regulated Utility Operations C. Risks Specific to Kentucky Regulated Segment D. Risks Specific to Pennsylvania Regulated Segment E. Risks Specific to Rhode Island Regulated Segment F. Risks Related to All Segments (PPL) A. Risk Related to Registrant Holding Company PPL is a holding company and its cash flows and ability to meet its obligations with respect to indebtedness and under guarantees, and its ability to pay dividends, largely depends on the financial performance of its respective subsidiaries and, as a result, is effectively subordinated to all existing and future liabilities of those subsidiaries. PPL is a holding company and conducts its operations primarily through subsidiaries. Substantially all of the consolidated assets of PPL are held by its subsidiaries. Accordingly, PPL's cash flows and ability to meet debt and guaranty obligations, as well as PPL's ability to pay dividends, are largely dependent upon the earnings of those subsidiaries and the distribution or other payment of such earnings in the form of dividends, distributions, loans, advances or repayment of loans and advances. The subsidiaries are separate legal entities and have no obligation to pay dividends or distributions to their parents or to make funds available for such a payment. The ability of PPL's subsidiaries to pay dividends or distributions in the future will depend on the subsidiaries' future earnings and cash flows and the needs of their businesses, and may be restricted by their obligations to holders of their outstanding debt and other creditors, as well as any contractual or legal restrictions in effect at such time, including the requirements of state corporate law applicable to payment of dividends and distributions, and regulatory requirements, including restrictions on the ability of PPL Electric, LG&E, KU, and RIE to pay dividends under Section 305(a) of the Federal Power Act. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers the common dividend more than three times over, so distributions to shareholders are funded from internally generated cash rather than incremental borrowing, a meaningful cushion for a holding company whose upstream dividends depend on subsidiary earnings.

Interest coverage improved year on year and sits modestly above the utilities sector median, reflecting operating income growth that outpaced the rise in gross interest expense as the rate base and revenue base expanded.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits above the sector median and edged higher year on year, leaving the issuer in the highly leveraged band with limited headroom; a modest EBITDA increase would be needed to reach the next lower band on a net-debt basis.

PPL is a holding company whose debt service and dividends depend on distributions from regulated subsidiaries, which are separate legal entities subject to Federal Power Act dividend restrictions and creditor claims, effectively subordinating holding-company obligations to subsidiary liabilities.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Capital expenditure exceeds operating cash flow, producing negative free cash flow and a negative free-cash-flow-to-debt ratio that is weaker than the sector median, so the build program is funded with balance-sheet debt rather than retained cash.

The debt note shows a syndicated facility maturing late in the decade with substantial unused capacity and a small bilateral facility expiring within the year; commercial paper is backstopped, but the near-term maturity ladder still requires routine refinancing.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged, with leverage above the sector median and cash-flow-to-debt below it; the credit view rests on regulated cash flows and continued access to committed facilities rather than on balance-sheet strength.

Our forward view is that leverage stays elevated while the capital program runs ahead of internally generated cash; coverage should hold near current levels, but a funding shortfall or adverse regulatory outcome would pressure the profile, and buyback data is unavailable.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流覆蓋普通股股息超過三倍，因此向股東作出的分派乃由內部產生的現金撥付，而非來自新增借貸；對於一家上游股息依賴附屬公司盈利的控股公司而言，這是重大的緩衝。
利息覆蓋率按年改善，並略高於公用事業行業中位數，反映營運收入增長快於總利息支出的上升，因費率基礎及收入基礎均有所擴大。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿高於行業中位數，並按年略為上升，使發行人處於高槓桿區間，餘裕有限；需要EBITDA溫和增長，方可在淨債務基礎上達到下一個較低區間。
PPL為控股公司，其償債及股息依賴受監管附屬公司的分派，而該等附屬公司為獨立法律實體，受《聯邦電力法》股息限制及債權人申索所規限，實際上使控股公司義務次於附屬公司負債。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 資本開支超過營運現金流，產生負自由現金流及負自由現金流對債務比率，且弱於行業中位數，因此建設計劃以資產負債表債務而非留存現金撥付。
債務附註顯示一項將於本十年末到期的銀團融資，尚有大量未動用額度，以及一項將於年內到期的小型雙邊融資；商業票據有備用支持，但近期到期階梯仍需例行再融資。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為高槓桿，槓桿高於行業中位數，而現金流對債務比率低於中位數；信貸觀點建基於受監管現金流及持續獲得承諾融資，而非資產負債表實力。
我們的前瞻觀點是，在資本計劃超前於內部產生現金的情況下，槓桿將維持高企；覆蓋率應維持於當前水平附近，但資金短缺或不利監管結果將對該狀況構成壓力，而回購數據無法取得。
